Eli (support): Hey @Ravi, saw your ticket about daily totals drifting between the Console chart and the CSV export. Can you paste a short repro?
Ravi @AcmeOps: Repro: Console shows 2026-03-10 = 12,034 tokens, but CSV export (download) has that activity on 2026-03-09. Our org timezone is Asia/Kolkata (UTC+5:30).
Eli (support): Thanks. Which view did you use to export (Usage > Daily -> Export CSV)?
Ravi @AcmeOps: Yep, Usage -> Daily -> Export CSV (default date range last 7 days). Also the per-route chart on the Dashboard snaps to 00:00 UTC for the day boundary. :confused:
Jamie (analytics): @Eli can you share the exact org_tz for Acme? And is the account legacy? Might be related to the old UTC cutover flag.
Eli (support): Acme org_tz = "Asia/Kolkata". Account created 2022-08-11. I can repro on staging with that org_tz.
Ravi @AcmeOps: attaching small snippet of exported CSV:
```
date,org_id,tokens
2026-03-09,acmeops,12034
2026-03-10,acmeops,0
```
Eli (support): Repro steps I used: 1) Set org_tz=Asia/Kolkata on staging account; 2) Send 12k tokens between 2026-03-09T18:30:00Z and 2026-03-09T19:15:00Z (which is 2026-03-10 00:00-00:45 IST); 3) Open Console -> Usage daily chart and Export CSV. Chart buckets by UTC day, export uses org_tz local day. Result: same tokens show up in different rows.
Jamie (analytics): Looks like mismatch is in the aggregation pipeline. Frontend chart uses precomputed daily_agg table truncated with date_trunc('day', ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') (so effectively UTC days), but the CSV export pipeline applies date_trunc('day', ts AT TIME ZONE org_tz). That explains off-by-one for non-UTC zones.
Maya (sre): InfraBot just posted a deploy at 2026-03-09 22:04UTC (release/2026-03-09-analytics-batching). Could that have changed default behavior? :eyes:
InfraBot: :rocket: Deployed release/2026-03-09-analytics-batching to prod at 2026-03-09T22:04:12Z (sha: a1b2c3).
Jamie (analytics): I inspected the migration PR. It added TZ normalization in the export job but didn't touch the frontend cache invalidation. So dashboards still read precomputed UTC-day aggregates. Regression happened because we now generate export-ready aggregates by org_tz but left the cached aggregates in UTC.
Eli (support): Short-term workaround for customers: set account flag `use_utc_midnight = false` to force exports and charts to align on org timezone, or temporarily set org_tz=UTC. I can toggle `use_utc_midnight` for Acme if they want.
Maya (sre): I'll open a rollback/patch ticket. Long-term fix: either store both agg keys (utc_day, local_day) in the agg table and surface the correct one in the frontend, or have the export job convert before writing CSV consistently.
Jamie (analytics): Proposed SQL for consistent aggregation (example):
```
SELECT
  org_id,
  date_trunc('day', timezone(org_tz, generated_at))::date AS local_day,
  sum(tokens) AS tokens
FROM events
GROUP BY org_id, local_day;
```
Eli (support): I'll message @Ravi with the temporary toggle. Ravi, want us to flip `use_utc_midnight` for your org now so numbers line up while we patch?
Ravi @AcmeOps: Yes please, flip it. That will help our finance team reconcile. Thanks!
Maya (sre): Filed SRE ticket SRE-2026-487: "analytics: align dashboard and export day-boundary with org timezone" and set priority P1 for rollout next week.
Eli (support): Noted. Follow-ups: 1) I'll flip the flag, confirm with Ravi when numbers match; 2) @Jamie will draft the aggregate migration; 3) @Maya will own rollout/patch.
Ravi @AcmeOps: Confirmed after flag flip — dashboard and CSV now show 2026-03-10 = 12,034. Appreciate the quick help! :tada:
Eli (support): Great — leaving SRE ticket open until patch is deployed. Thanks everyone.
